properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-20.

HIS WORDS: "allow a user to map out tasks in discretized increments (potentially, a manager could say, task package 1 is Alex's, task package 2 is AJ's, and so on)."

THIS IS A WORK BREAKDOWN STRUCTURE, and it is worth naming as such because it is standard practice in exactly the world he comes from. A WBS slices an increment into packages, each with a single accountable owner. It is the artifact a manager actually manages with, and it is what makes 'who is behind?' answerable.

WHAT REFLOW2 ALREADY HAS, and none of the three is this:
  · OWNED_BY — whose AREA this is. Durable, standing, never released. About a REGION of the design, not a bundle of work.
  · CLAIMS — who is IN it right now. Transient, advisory, session-scoped, released at checkout.
  · AUTHORED_BY (role=approver) — who was ASKED to settle a decision. The only thing loop_status attributes today.

A work package is none of those. It is a SCOPED BUNDLE OF WORK, inside an increment, with one accountable person, that exists until it is delivered. Standing like ownership, but about work rather than area; scoped like a claim, but durable and assigned rather than self-taken.

WHY IT MIGHT MATTER MORE THAN IT LOOKS: the graph today can answer 'what is owed?' design-wide and 'what needs this person?' only for decisions they were asked to settle. It cannot answer 'what is Alex's slice of increment 3, and is it done?' — which is the question a manager asks every week. `loop_status(contributor_id)` already reports that most debt classes are `not_attributable`, which is the honest version of the same absence.

OPTIONS, none chosen:
  (a) A NEW EDGE on the existing schedule — SCHEDULED_FOR already carries `modality`; a package identifier plus an owner could ride alongside. Cheapest, no new node type. Weak: a package is a THING a manager names and talks about, and a property on an edge cannot be named or discussed.
  (b) A WORK PACKAGE NODE contained by the increment, with capabilities and requirements scheduled into IT rather than directly into the epoch, and OWNED_BY the person. Most faithful to how WBS actually works, and it makes 'Alex's slice' a node you can ask about. Costs a schema addition and a level of indirection.
  (c) REUSE OWNED_BY over a claimed region — no schema change at all, and claim_region can already describe a region by a query. Weak: ownership is about AREA and is never released, while a package is finished and closed; and a region defined by a query is not a set of tasks somebody agreed to do.
  (d) DO NOTHING and let a manager keep the slicing outside reflow2. Honest option, and the status quo.

COUNTER-ARGUMENT, recorded beside the idea: reflow2 has deliberately kept people OUT of the blast radius — AUTHORED_BY, CLAIMS and OWNED_BY are all excluded from traceability so that a change never propagates into a person. Work packages are the point at which a design tool starts becoming a project-management tool, and that is a boundary worth crossing deliberately rather than by accident. The countervailing fact: `req:people-are-modellable-inside-the-design` is already an open requirement asking for organisation, role and who-performs-a-function, so the door is not closed.

RELATED: dec:idea-lining-work-up-in-increments-should-be-the-default-not-a-skill-you-remember.
properties.name: OPEN — can an increment be sliced into discrete work packages, each with a named owner, so a manager can say "package 1 is Alex's, package 2 is AJ's"?
